statements.status_notes: CVE-2022-3219: gpg can be made to spin on a small input, for example a public key with thousands of signatures attached and compressed down to a few kilobytes (https://dev.gnupg.org/T5993, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2127010). Upstream GnuPG declined the proposed general change. In 2025 it added a narrower one, 'gpg: Do not allow compressed key packets on import' (https://github.com/gpg/gnupg/commit/23ccad05c68005b580c7b209e2242bb93893af62), which is not in the 2.4.7 release. Debian's trixie gnupg2 package, 2.4.7-21+deb13u1, applies the FreePG patch 'Disallow compressed signatures and certificates' by Demi Marie Obenour, the change proposed for this CVE under GnuPG bug T5993. When parsing keys it returns an error on a compressed packet instead of decompressing it, it accepts only signature and marker packets in detached signatures, and it rejects partial-length and indeterminate-length packets in keys and signatures. Debian's tracker still lists trixie as unfixed (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2022-3219). This owner is built from Debian 2.4.7-21+deb13u1, and both builds now in the DHI Debian repository are rebuilds of that version. In both, the gpg and gpgv binaries on amd64 and arm64 carry the patch's new error messages for partial-length and indeterminate-length packets in keyrings and detached signatures and for packet types not allowed in detached signatures; the GnuPG 2.4.7 release sources have none of them. Every rebuild of 2.4.7-21+deb13u1 carries the patch, so the range closes at the first one.
